clues: This city lies on a wide gulf on the Tyrrhenian Sea in south Italy. It is the main town of its own province in the Campania lands.
A strong wind pours down from the hills to the gulf, most of all in winter. Yet this town still ranks among the most sunny in Italy.
From February to August 1944, this city held the seat of the nation's rule. Two war time cabinets worked from a grand marble hall in the town.
Long ago this city held one of the first medical schools in Europe. Many call it a seed from which the new kind of university grew.
The relics of Saint Matthew rest in a crypt in the town church. He is one of the town patron saints, kept with great honor.
